 Medium
 Large
 Print NEW DELHI: The dust is yet to settle on the controversy-marred SOM elections, but the next battle for control of Indian Olympic Association (IOA) has already begun. And this time, the real power play will unfold among the national sports federations (NSFs), whose representatives could hold the key to determining who calls the shots in the Olympic body for the 2026-2030 term. Soon after the SOM polls, returning officer Sanjay K Srivastava has notified the initial election schedule, inviting eligible NSFs to nominate their authorised representatives, one male and one female, who will constitute the electoral college and become part of the IOA General Assembly for the Olympic body's Dec 5 polls. The provisional electoral college is scheduled for Nov 12, with the final electoral roll to be published on Nov 15. Join conversation

 ALSO READ: PT Usha takes IOA election battle to IOC, seeks independent probe into alleged violations The nominations will offer the first real glimpse of where the federations' loyalties lie. Their nominees will not merely be there to cast votes; some could themselves emerge as contenders for key office-bearer and executive council (EC) positions. In other words, the battle lines are now being drawn. However, not everyone has made it to the starting grid. Prominently missing is the Boxing Federation of India (BFI), effectively shutting out its representatives from the IOA electoral process amid factional infighting and legal disputes. The IOA does not currently recognise BFI as a member and had earlier rejected its nominees, Nikhat Zareen and Narendra Berwal, for the Athletes' Commission elections. The Indian Golf Union (IGU), Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI) and Volleyball Federation (VFI) are also absent owing to administrative issues. With just 30 NSFs making the cut, the electoral arithmetic is already taking shape.
